subject: biology
title: The lungs and gas exchange
key_idea: Air passes down the trachea and bronchi to the alveoli. Oxygen diffuses from the alveoli into the blood, and carbon dioxide diffuses the other way. Alveoli are adapted for fast diffusion: a large surface area, thin walls and a good blood supply.

blocks.text: The lungs are the organs where gas exchange takes place. This section covers the parts you need to know.

diagram.alt: Tap a part of the breathing system to learn its job, then test yourself.

parts.name: Trachea
parts.detail: The windpipe. It carries air down from the mouth and nose towards the lungs.

parts.name: Bronchi
parts.detail: Two tubes that branch from the trachea, one to each lung.

parts.name: Alveoli
parts.detail: Tiny air sacs at the ends of the tubes. This is where gas exchange takes place.

parts.name: Capillary network
parts.detail: A network of tiny blood vessels around each alveolus. It brings carbon dioxide to the lungs and takes oxygen away.

items: Air travels down the trachea and bronchi to the alveoli.
Gas exchange happens in the alveoli.
The right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs, where gas exchange takes place.

blocks.text: Gases move between the alveoli and the blood by diffusion. Each gas moves from where it is in a high concentration to where it is in a low concentration.

items: Oxygen is used in respiration. The blood arriving at the lungs has a low concentration of oxygen, so oxygen diffuses into it.
Carbon dioxide is produced by respiration. The blood arriving has a high concentration, so it diffuses out into the air.
Gases pass through a membrane. The wall of the alveolus and the wall of the capillary are each only one cell thick.

diagram.alt: Change the concentration of oxygen in the alveolus and in the blood and watch the concentration difference. A bigger difference means faster diffusion.

items: Oxygen diffuses from the alveolus into the blood.
Carbon dioxide diffuses from the blood into the alveolus.
A bigger concentration difference makes diffusion faster.

blocks.text: Each adaptation makes diffusion faster. Always say what the feature does.

rows: A large surface area for gas exchange
Walls of the alveolus and capillary are one cell thick
Capillary network around each alveolus (a good blood supply)
Takes oxygen away and brings carbon dioxide quickly, which maintains the concentration gradient
Ventilation (breathing moves air in and out)
Brings in fresh oxygen and removes carbon dioxide, which maintains the concentration gradient

blocks.text: In the narrowest capillaries, red blood cells pass one at a time. This reduces the distance for diffusion and slows the blood, giving more time for oxygen to be taken up.

items: Large surface area, thin walls and a good blood supply.
Ventilation and blood flow keep the concentration gradient steep.
Link each feature to a faster rate of diffusion.

checks.q: Name the gas that diffuses from the blood into the alveolus.
Give two ways that the lungs are adapted for efficient gas exchange.
checks.a: Any two from: many alveoli giving a large surface area; wall of the alveolus one cell thick; wall of the capillary one cell thick; good blood supply; well ventilated.

checks.q: Explain why a good blood supply helps gas exchange.
checks.a: It removes oxygenated blood quickly and brings carbon dioxide to the lungs quickly, which maintains a concentration gradient.

worked_example.question:
Gas exchange happens in the alveoli in the lungs.

Describe three features of the alveoli that help maximise gas exchange.
answer_points: Large surface area, or large surface area to volume ratio.
(Large) capillary network, or many capillaries, or a good or efficient blood supply.
Walls are thin or one cell thick.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each feature. Say the wall is thin. Moist, steep concentration gradient and "thin cell walls" do not score.

worked_example.question:
Gas exchange happens in the alveoli in the lungs.

The capillary wall is only one cell thick.

Explain how gases move from the alveolus to the capillary.
answer_points: Down a concentration gradient, from a high concentration to a low concentration.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each of the three points.

items: The surface of the alveoli is moist.
Oxygen and carbon dioxide dissolve in the moisture, so they can move across into the blood.
Breathing keeps a high concentration of oxygen and a low concentration of carbon dioxide in the alveoli.

worked_example.question:
The human circulatory system is described as a double circulatory system.

Explain why.
answer_points: Blood travels through the pump (heart) twice.
On one full circuit around the body.

Also allowed: there are two pumps; blood passes separately to the lungs and to the body, in a pulmonary circuit and a systemic circuit; or a description: the blood goes through the heart to the lungs, returns to the heart, and then goes to the rest of the body.
worked_example.tip: A full description of the route, heart to lungs, back to the heart, then to the body, scores both marks.

items: The pulmonary circuit takes blood from the heart to the lungs, where gas exchange happens, and back to the heart.
The systemic circuit takes blood from the heart to the rest of the body and back to the heart.
Blood passes through the heart twice on one full circuit of the body.
Advantages: the heart increases the pressure of the blood a second time, so it flows faster and more oxygen reaches the tissues.
